artworks.title: Echo and Narcissus
artworks.description: Waterhouse pairs the fading nymph with the boy at the spring — Echo's last embrace refused, Nemesis' answer still to come.

artworks.title: Narcissus
artworks.description: Caravaggio isolates Ovid's hunter at the pool: a single figure bent over his own reflection, knee and sleeve catching the only light in an otherwise black void. Desire and doom collapse into one circular composition — the youth already trapped by the image that will waste him into a flower. Oil on canvas, Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica (Palazzo Barberini), Rome.

artworks.title: Echo and Narcissus
artworks.description: Poussin's classical pastoral shows Narcissus already fading by the water while Echo collapses in grief and a putto mourns nearby — Ovid's metamorphosis rendered as ordered landscape tragedy. The youth who loved only himself becomes part of the still pool that destroyed him. Oil on canvas, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Echo Flying from Narcissus
artworks.description: The English Neoclassical painter Guy Head makes Echo the fleeing protagonist: she turns from the self-absorbed youth at the spring, her rejected love already driving her into the woods where only her voice will remain. Oil on canvas, Detroit Institute of Arts.

popCulture.title: Narcissism
popCulture.description: The clinical and everyday name for self-absorbed desire — Ovid's pool still supplying the West's vocabulary of the mirror.
